subject: Appeal: missing trial credits — multiple team signups (Compasslytics)
body:
From: Zachary Kim <zach.kim@compasslytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Shaw <olivia.shaw@compasslytics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Missing trial credits for new teammates — please help

Hi Ben,

We just onboarded a handful of engineers to test Redwood for a week and several of them signed up but did not receive the free trial credits. I pulled the account emails and IDs below — none have cards attached, this was purely self-serve. Can you check why credits weren't granted? We need to run a short eval this week.

Accounts:
- olivia.shaw@compasslytics.com (acc_9812)
- j.patel@compasslytics.com (acc_9813)
- c.gonzalez@compasslytics.com (acc_9814)
- t.sanders@compasslytics.com (acc_9815)

I attached a screenshot of the signup confirmation pages we saw. Happy to provide more info.

Thanks,
Zach
Security & Ops, Compasslytics

-----Original Message-----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Zachary Kim <zach.kim@compasslytics.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Missing trial credits for new teammates — please help

Hi Zach — really appreciate the quick flag.

Short answer: some self-serve grants get auto-blocked by our abuse heuristics; we saw a small cluster linked to Compasslytics signups that tripped controls this morning. I'm looping in our ops and fraud triage folks (Avery, Monica) to take a closer look and confirm whether credits were correctly withheld.

Next steps I will take now:
- Ask ops for session / cookie logs for the listed account IDs.
- Hold any manual issuance until we confirm (won't penalize legitimate users).
- Follow up with you within a few hours with an interim update.

If you have any recent IP ranges or corp NAT info that might make these look noisy, send that over.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 3, 2028 at 11:02 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
> To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
> Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
> Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 11:02:37 -0700
> Subject: Re: Missing trial credits for new teammates — please help
>
> Ben / Monica — quick triage notes from our initial pass:
>
> - I pulled the signups for the four account IDs Zach shared. They were all created within a 7-minute window (09:05–09:12 PDT).
> - Session evidence: all four accounts show the same long session cookie ID (hashed: sess_4b2a8c7d) being replayed across distinct account creations. Cookie TTLs and UA strings are different enough to appear like different browsers, but the cookie value is identical and the cookie origin header traces back to a single frontend edge with the same client fingerprint nonce.
> - IP evidence: the connecting IPs resolve to the same /24 subnet but are different addresses (likely cloud VMs). Reverse DNS shows common cloud provider names, not Compasslytics corporate ranges.
> - Browser fingerprint: UA string similarity score is 92% across the samples, but image-based UA headers differ; screenshot attached (ua-similarity-screenshot.png).
> - There is an appeal PDF attached to the external email (attempted to attach to their support form) — included here for record.
>
> Preliminary assessment: this looks like cookie replay / session reuse across multiple signups — consistent with scripted or proxied signups (bot farm / session-sharing). Given that, our auto-block likely operated correctly on the initial issuance rule (cookie replay + rapid multi-creates).
>
> Recommended immediate actions:
> 1) Keep credits on hold for the four suspicious accounts.
> 2) Run a quick verification call with Zach/Olivia to gather corporate NAT ranges and confirm these emails really map to Compasslytics employees.
> 3) If Compasslytics proves ownership, we can issue manual credits to verified employee emails only; do not bulk-issue.
> 4) Send the cluster to security for a deeper look (possible automated signups using a captured session token).
>
> Monica — can you pull the full session replay logs and check for additional account IDs that share sess_4b2a? If this cookie is in use elsewhere, we may have a broader wave to contend with. I attached a CSV export of the cluster I pulled (session-cluster.csv).
>
> -Avery
> Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
>
> On Mon, Sep 3, 2028 at 15:42 Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
>
> > From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
> > To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
> > Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Zachary Kim <zach.kim@compasslytics.com>
> > Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 15:42:10 -0700
> > Subject: Re: Missing trial credits for new teammates — please help
> >
> > Thanks for the details, Avery. I pulled the session-store and correlated the cookie hash. Findings:
> >
> > - The sess_4b2a8c7d value appears in 27 account creation events over the last 48 hours across 3 distinct customer domains. 18 of those were blocked by our heuristics; 9 were allowed (older windows).
> > - Timing pattern: 70% of creations linked to that cookie occur in tight bursts (6–12 accounts in <10 minutes).
> > - There are traces of a reused client-side localStorage key (lf_nonce) being copied across signups — classic client-side session cloning.
> > - No payment-type metadata for these accounts; they were clearly self-serve trials.
> >
> > Recommendation: classify the Compasslytics cluster as high risk. We should:
> > a) Deny auto-issuance for the flagged IDs and document the appeal as "rejected — session replay evidence".
> > b) Offer a remediation path to Compasslytics: a short verification call and then manual issuance of a one-off promo credit to confirmed employee accounts (limit 2 accounts max).
> > c) Kick off a security incident if we see the cookie used against additional enterprise customers (I will flag to secops).
> >
> > Ben — if you want to proceed with a verification call, I can join. Zach / Olivia — if you can provide a short list of corporate outbound IP ranges or confirm that those emails are managed by you, we can move faster.
> >
> > Monica Patel
> > Fraud & Risk Analyst, Redwood Inference
> >
> > -----
> > Attachment stubs: session-cluster.csv (CSV, 12 KB); ua-similarity-screenshot.png (PNG, 140 KB); appeal-form-Compasslytics.pdf (PDF, 28 KB)
